revision_notes: A single check found clear, authoritative evidence contradicting the Unknown score: Revenue Services Lesotho (RSL) publishes official e-Taxation and e-Payments platform guides describing an operational online portal (rsl.org.ls) where taxpayers file CIT, IIT, RIIT, T&E, VAT and PAYE returns and pay directly via mobile money or bank digital channels, with Standard Lesotho Bank's Unayo app posting payments to RSL in real time. revised_comments: Revenue Services Lesotho (RSL) operates an official e-Taxation (e-Filing) portal at rsl.org.ls where taxpayers register online to file and amend Company Income Tax, Individual Income Tax, Resident Individual Income Tax, Trust & Estate, VAT and PAYE returns, and view real-time balances. Payment is made through the linked RSL e-Payments platform using mobile money (EcoCash, M-Pesa via USSD or app) or, for Standard Lesotho Bank customers, the Unayo app/internet banking/USSD/agents, which reflects payments in the RSL system immediately; payments via other commercial banks require the taxpayer to upload proof of payment.

Definition: Whether the instant payment system is used or can be used for government disbursements to citizens, including social transfers, welfare payments, salaries, pensions, subsidies, grants, and emergency assistance.
Comments: Value=0 (unknown) because I did not find credible, specific evidence that Government of Lesotho social transfers/salaries are actively disbursed via a national digital payment system/mobile money at scale; searches returned general social assistance project information without specifying payment rails used (bank vs mobile money vs cash). Searched: "Lesotho government to person payments mobile money", "Child Grant Programme payment method Lesotho", "G2P Lesotho mobile money".
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: A single check surfaced clear, specific, and dated evidence that G2P mobile disbursement is under way (UN Lesotho Policy Watch Jan 2025, EU/UNICEF release, Government of Lesotho MGYSACS notice, World Bank G2PX project document), directly contradicting the 'no specific evidence' basis for the Unknown score. This row was mislabelled; recalculated to 2 (Limited Use) reflecting partial, expanding rollout rather than full active use.
revised_comments: The Government of Lesotho, supported by the EU, UNICEF and the World Bank (G2PX project), is progressively shifting government-to-person disbursements from manual cash-in-transit to mobile money. The Child Grants Programme, Old Age Pension and Public Assistance are being migrated to payment via M-Pesa and EcoCash, with elderly and vulnerable beneficiaries enrolled from August 2023 and over 13,000 beneficiaries reported receiving grants via mobile platforms by early 2025. Use of the digital rail for G2P remains partial and geographically phased rather than the default channel for all social transfers, salaries or pensions.

revised_comments: The Central Bank of Lesotho (CBL) publishes payment system performance data annually through its statutory Annual Report and its Financial Stability Report (issued each March), covering metrics such as Lesotho Wire (RTGS) transaction volumes and values, system availability rates, and mobile money sector growth trends. The CBL's Payment System Oversight Framework (2018) formally commits the Bank to an annual oversight report, summarised in its main Annual Report, supplemented by internal quarterly performance monitoring that is not separately published.

revision_notes: A single check found the primary legal instruments governing payment system audits (2017 e-money issuer regulations; Payment Systems Act 2014), which mandate independent, CBL-approved audits and permit special audits, but no evidence that results are made public. This row was mislabelled as unresearchable; recalculated to 2 (Private Audits) rather than left Unknown.
revised_comments: Lesotho's Payment Systems (Issuers of Electronic Payment Instruments) Regulations 2017 require every licensed e-money/payment instrument issuer to appoint an independent auditor approved by the Central Bank of Lesotho (CBL), submit annual audited financial statements within three months of financial year-end, and undergo CBL-ordered special audits where irregularities are suspected. The Payment Systems Act 2014 additionally empowers the CBL itself to inspect and audit payment system operators and participants. These audits are conducted and reported to the regulator, but findings are not published, so reviews remain private rather than publicly disclosed.
